I'll just copy/paste:

I just did this a couple weeks ago so it's pretty fresh.
This is the YouTube video I used as my basis: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j7jvQscuVBo . It's outdated now but the basics are still spot on.
(Here's a recent video. I didn't really use many of these methods but it might give you some ideas. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3qjuUA4FvV8 )
Instead of detailing everything I did, I'm just going to point what I did differently than he does in that video. It's just easier that way. This video was made before TTK so we have access to more powerful and varied weapons.
First, I did this with my Hunter. It's definitely doable with any of the classes from what I've seen, though. Also, I was 335 when I did this so damage output will vary depending on your level.
During the lamps, I ran Bladedancer. The most important perk is the one that turn you invisible when you crouch. I also used the perk that lets you use R2 to turn invisible during your super. Additionally, I also wore the Don't Touch Me gauntlets. Basically, you can be invisible the whole time. Super easy. I did initially try doing the jump cheese that he shows in the video but simply could not do it consistently. I'm sure someone could point out exactly what I was doing wrong but the invis way is very low risk so I'm happy with it.
At the next section, I switched to Nightstalker for the triple jump and also equipped my Bones of Eao. Jumping the gap is super easy with a Hunter. Just make sure you space your jumps out to get maximum height. (I also hear holding the jump button makes you jump higher. Not 100% sure if that's true but I do it anyway.) Once you're at the height of your jump, mash the melee button to sword-swing the rest of the way as you see in the video.
I switched back to my Bladedancer and Don't Touch Me's at this point and patiently picked off the wizards and ogres as they come out with my 1KYS.
Stay on Bladedancer. Equip your Sleeper Simulant. The following part can be tricky. I died here a couple times.
I passed the thrallway pretty much like you see in the video. The difference is, with the Sleeper you can one-shot the shriekers even when they're closed. So don't even bother to wait for them to open just blast away and run away from the purple blasts. Make liberal use of your invisibility here because those thrall can overwhelm you quick.
I switched back to my Nightstalker and re-equipped Bones. I kept my Sleeper equipped but this part is viable with Raze Lighter and a sniper.
I also just stood there and waited for my grenades to recharge just in case I needed them (particularly the invisibility smoke bomb). In the video, he tosses a grenade up under the wizards in that first hallway but that's no longer necessary.
You'll see he baits the Hallowed Wizards out of their rooms. That's not necessary, either. It takes two Sleeper shots to kill the wizards. I just ran and immediately killed them as soon as they passed through the barrier. Then with my third Sleeper shot I'd kill the shrieker. (Again, don't wait for it to open, just blast it.) Then I'd run away to the elevated room across the way (where he kills the wizard in the video) and let the purple blasties disintegrate. The second video shows how the guy uses his Raze Lighter. I personally found the shrieker to be the greater threat and wanted to take them out quickly so I preferred the Sleeper for that reason.
Rinse and repeat on the other side.
The Deathsinger can be a little tricky. When the countdown starts - or when you feel safe enough to push in - tether the Deathsinger and shoot away with your Sleeper. Using the spot shown in the video to shoot him is good. I also found that going into the same room and jumping on top of one of the doorways also provided me enough cover. I think I died here once or twice so be careful. Once he's down, the time pressure's off so just invis, run away, regroup, and clear adds until Crota appears.
I beat Crota pretty much as seen in the video except I used Telesto instead of the methods he shows. It takes three Telesto shots to down him. The idea is that it provides just enough to delay on that third shot where I can jump up and get in position.
In reality, I'd be willing to bet that Raze Lighter is the superior option here based on OP's video. If I were to do it again, I'd use Raze Lighter.
The Swordbearer should go down quick. I just tethered him and machine gunned him. Seems like with Raze Lighter you can kill him with one uppercut.
As for Crota, just be safe. His shield doesn't stay down long. If you're getting too hurt, just bail. Don't go for that last hit. I had a run where I was literally one sword strike away from killing him but got killed by a boomer. I should've just run away and gone another cycle. Took me months before I even attempted it again because I was so heartbroken.
The most important thing is to stay calm. This is easier than you think and is absolutely doable. I'd say if you're the type who spends time on /r/destinythegame then you are definitely capable of this. Good luck! If you have specific questions about certain areas or encounters I'm always happy to provide insight.
